title: Recording: Backwards Traveller by Wings | 1977
content:
Studio Two, Abbey Road Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Geoff Emerick

Wings recorded the London Town song ‘Backwards Traveller’ on 11 November 1977.

They had attempted to record the song two days before, but had been unable to complete a master take. They did so during this session.

The basic track had Paul McCartney on drums, Denny Laine on acoustic guitar, and Linda McCartney on keyboards. Paul then added more acoustic guitar, plus bass guitar and synthesizer parts, the latter providing the underwater sounds heard during the song. He then overdubbed his lead vocals, followed by backing vocals by all three members of Wings.

Most of the album was the line-up that was when we went to America, with Jimmy and Joe, but there’s a couple of the tracks on it that we did after they’d left, like ‘Backwards Traveller’ and ‘Cuff Link’ where, like, I drummed, for instance, and a couple of tracks I played guitar on, which I mightn’t have done if Jimmy had still been with us.
Paul McCartney
An Evening With Paul McCartney, Capitol Radio, 21 March 1978

Rough mixes of eight London Town recordings were made before the end of the session: ‘Children Children’, ‘I’ve Had Enough’, ‘Backwards Traveller’, ‘Cuff Link’, ‘Deliver Your Children’, ‘London Town’, ‘Don’t Let It Bring You Down’, and ‘Famous Groupies’.

That evening, a launch party was held in London for ‘Mull Of Kintyre’.
